newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH, SWEDISH BEET TESTS SHOW MIXED YIELDS.
newsitem.headline: DANISH, SWEDISH BEET TESTS SHOW MIXED YIELDS.

text.p: Results of Denmark's first beet tests conducted on August 11 and issued by sole producer Danisco A/S on Wednesday showed 37.1 tonnes per hectare versus an average of 30.4 over the past five years with sugar content at 15.1 percent (15.6).
Figures for Sweden were 29.0 (27.5) tonnes/hectare and sugar content of 15.5 percent (16.0).

A Danisco statement predicted combined sugar production for whole year 1997 would be well above its European Union quota of some 920,000 tonnes for all three countries provided the present growing season continued with sun and adequate rain.

Danisco forecast production levels for Denmark for the whole year 1997 to be at least at 1996's level of around 504,000 tonnes, exceeding 1996's 398,000 tonnes in Sweden but below last year's approximate 146,000 tonnes in eastern Germany.
Danisco's EU sugar production quota this year splits up into 425,000 tonnes for Denmark, 370,000 tonnes for Sweden and 126,000 tonnes for Germany.
It said that both the time of sowing and conditions so far pointed to "very favourable development" of beets this season.

"Based on the good spring establishment and the favourable weather conditions of the growing period with a good combination of sun and rain, it is estimated that beets in Denmark, Sweden and Germany have a good growth potential," Danisco said in its statement.
It said sugar percentages might not be as high in 1997 as in 1996 but root growth was better.
Danisco, with a virtual monopoly of production in Denmark and Sweden as well as its operation in Germany, is Europe's fourth biggest sugar producer.
